title: Alexander Wolitzky, MIT 14.121: Lectures 1–2, Choice, Preference, and Utility (2015)
use: Method reference for complete/transitive preferences, ordinal representations, continuity, monotonicity/local nonsatiation, convex/strictly convex preferences and quasiconcavity; complete-choice-correspondence WARP convention.
verification: Retrieved the actual 33-page official MIT lecture PDF and inspected numbered slides7–16 and20–27, including the formal correspondence WARP definition on slide11, strictly increasing representation rule, finite versus infinite representation distinction, LNS and the upper-contour/quasiconcavity statements. Used only these stable method passages. The chapter supplies original definitions/examples and proofs, does not copy source exercises or assert the source's wider rationalization/representation theorems without their full hypotheses, and does not rely on the later separability section.

title: Ted Bergstrom, UCSB Economics 210A: Notes on Revealed Preference (17 November 2016)
use: Author-hosted primary notes on conventional budget WARP, the problem of tied choices, strict affordability under local nonsatiation and longer revealed-preference chains.
verification: Retrieved and read the actual three-page PDF text. Page1 gives the traditional no-reversal condition; page2 explicitly discusses ties and defines strict direct revealed preference using strict affordability; page3 distinguishes the pairwise tie-permitting condition from longer-chain restrictions. The manuscript states both conventions through precise inequalities and proves its necessary implications independently. It does not repeat the note's apparent final-clause typo in the strict-affordability explanation, copy its referenced workbook exercise, or invoke its broad finite-data rationalization claim as an unproved chapter theorem. A screenshot fetch of this PDF later returned a cache miss; the full text retrieval was successful and is the basis of the scoped source inspection.
